headline: Aug 9 got skipped entirely and that was the right call — today stays a genuine easy run while load and sleep debt still clear.
body_state: Garmin's live readiness score is 11 (very low) despite HRV reading BALANCED (38ms) and body battery at 46 — training status is "Recovery". Sleep was 6.4h (score 72), adding to a 26h/14-day debt. The composite verdict (score 51.1, band moderate) reads friendlier because TSB (-23) sits in the productive-training zone, but it still flags **red**: acute:chronic load 2.27 (>1.5 = 2–4x injury risk next week) and the sleep debt itself. Garmin's own number is the more conservative read today — trust it over the composite.
session: **5km Easy Run** — 4.9km @ 4:35–5:03/km, cutback week. The point is the volume drop, not this run: conversational, RPE 3-4, finish feeling like you could go again. Cadence cue carries over from Aug 7's analysis — aim 168-172 spm, don't let stride do the work. If HR creeps toward 75% max (~146bpm), slow down rather than hold pace.
recent: Aug 7's "easy" long run wasn't — it closed at 179bpm/4:11 pace, threshold-adjacent, and readiness cratered to 23 right after. Aug 8's Un1t class landed green (42min, full dose, TE 2.8/2.1 aerobic/anaerobic) with no RPE logged yet. Aug 9 — both the Un1t hybrid and outdoor cycling — went unrun, and that gap is exactly what a readiness-gated rest day should look like given the week's ACWR spike. Net effect: still digging out, but the hole stopped getting deeper.
focus: Run today genuinely easy — cap effort well short of Aug 7's threshold drift.
Log RPE on Aug 8's Un1t class (and any HYROX-style sessions) so session-RPE load stops relying on HR alone.
Protect sleep before Wednesday's 5K Time Trial (Aug 12) — an honest recalibration number needs a rested body, not a 26h-debt one.
